content: 1. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Co-administration of cobicistat with atazanavir and indinavir is contraindicated due to the risk of indirect (unconjugated) hyperbilirubinemia. 3. Indinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 4. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination requires close monitoring. 5. Indinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases infigratinib levels via the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 9. HIV protease inhibitors, including darunavir, may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and induce hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely. 10. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, inhaled insulin, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Co-administration of cobicistat with atazanavir and irinotecan is contraindicated. 13. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Co-administration of isavuconazonium sulfate with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 16. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Ivosidenib decreases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative drugs. 22. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Darunavir and ixazomib interact via CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 24. Cobicistat and ixazomib interact via CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 25. Darunavir decreases the plasma levels or effects of ketamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Cobicistat and ketoconazole increase each other’s plasma levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 27. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 28. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of lacosamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative drugs. 31. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Lenacapavir increases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Lenacapavir increases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Letermovir increases the plasma levels of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Cobicistat increases the plasma levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 45. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 46. Cobicistat and levoketoconazole increase each other’s plasma levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 47. Levoketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Darunavir increases the plasma levels or effects of levoketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
